Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, Asia-Pacific, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    US airstrikes on Iran triggered a broad risk-off move across global markets. Oil (Brent ~$95.45) surged on Strait of Hormuz disruption fears, driving inflation anxiety. Global bonds sold off sharply — US 10Y yield hit 4.8122% (near 3-year high), JGB 10Y at 3.015% (3-decade high). Asian equities fell hard (KOSPI -4%, Nikkei -2.9%). Wall Street also declined (S&P -0.7%, Nasdaq -1%). Fed rate hike odds for the Sep 16 meeting jumped to 67% from 39.6% a week prior. RBNZ hiked 25bps but struck a dovish tone. USD firmed. Gold, BTC, ETH all slightly lower.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — covers US yields at near 3-year highs, Fed hike probability, S&P/Nasdaq moves, ISM manufacturing data, and Fed funds futures pricing.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 67% (per CME FedWatch, 25bps hike at Sep 16 meeting)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (marginally — a hike is noted as "not certain," leaving room for a hold)
Probability of holding: 33% (implied residual from CME FedWatch)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — no discussion of cuts whatsoever)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (Meaningfully hawkish — hike odds nearly doubled in one week to 67%, 10Y yield at multi-year highs, geopolitical inflation shock reinforcing the case for further Fed tightening; only modest offset is that a hike remains not fully priced)
